Research direction

Intelligence for physical infrastructure.

My work connects visual perception with embedded control and robotics in renewable-energy applications. The question guiding this direction is:

How can robotics, computer vision and embedded intelligence make the inspection, maintenance and operation of renewable-energy infrastructure more autonomous, reliable and scalable?

Selected work

Projects built around sensing, intelligence and control.

Solar panel cleaning rover

Flagship project · BRAC University

SPICS: Solar Panel Inspection & Cleaning Systems

An integrated solar-maintenance system combining UAV-based inspection, deep-learning classification and detection, embedded control and a semi-autonomous cleaning rover. EPSRG publicly documents the project as the Best Project among ten Summer 2024 FYDP groups and describes a ground-station workflow connecting aerial inspection, dirty-panel identification and targeted cleaning.

Project evaluation

Test-bed capacities are reported per battery charge.

315Test-bed panels cleaned per rover charge, as reported by EPSRGEach mark represents one test-bed panel.
75Test-bed panels inspected per UAV charge, as reported by EPSRGEach mark represents one test-bed panel.
79%Custom CNN accuracy on the reported 200-image test set
90.1%Precision for detecting the “Dusty” class in the reported evaluation

Engineering completeness: EPSRG reports water cleaning, waterless cleaning, targeted-panel cleaning and scheduled-cleaning modes. The internal FYDP economic model estimated an approximately 52-day payback under its highest-dust savings assumption, which is presented as a modeled scenario rather than a field-validated commercial claim.

Current lab context

Industrial-scale solar maintenance research

EPSRG’s ongoing portfolio includes an industrial-grade automated cleaning system for BRAC University’s 1.4 MW rooftop PV plant and a UAV-based solar inspection system using aerial imaging and thermal analysis. Both are listed as funded by the Department of Operations, BRAC University.

These are group-level programmes. This portfolio attributes specific responsibilities to Ifty only where his CV, certificates or project records separately support them.

Research trajectory

From connected systems to intelligent solar maintenance.

01 / 06Research FoundationIoT, AI & applied technology research
01 Research02 Control03 Vision04 Robotics05 Energy06 R&D
01Research Foundation

IoT, AI & Applied Technology Research

At Pathfinder Research and Consultancy Center, my work on IoT applications in smart agriculture and AI in healthcare led to first-authored peer-reviewed reviews. Literature synthesis and technical writing established a systems-level approach to applied technology.

02Closing the Loop

Embedded Systems & Control

ATMega32 traffic-management and LM35 temperature-control projects moved that systems approach into sensing, decision logic and actuation. Servo control, relay operation and closed-loop feedback made physical system response the central concern.

03From Sensing to Perception

Computer Vision & Deep Learning

For street-sign detection in Dhaka, I curated and annotated an image dataset using CVAT, trained YOLO-based models in Python and Google Colab, and evaluated precision, recall, IoU and mAP. Visual perception added a learned interpretation of the environment to earlier control work.

04Perception Meets Robotics

SPICS: Solar Panel Inspection & Cleaning System

SPICS connected aerial imaging, clean-versus-dusty classification, IoT communication and a semi-autonomous cleaning rover. The engineering challenge shifted toward integrating perception, decision-making and actuation in one working system.

05From Prototype to Research

Renewable Energy, Agrivoltaics & Research Assistantship

Part-time agrivoltaic research at BRAC University broadened the context around robotics before my return to SPICS as a full-time Research Assistant. PV performance, environmental conditions, operating constraints, economics and scalability became part of the engineering question.

06Current Convergence

Intelligent Solar Maintenance R&D

Continuing solar-maintenance R&D brings feedback control and photovoltaic perception into the same research direction. The emphasis is now on repeatability, maintainability and system integration, with deployment as a research objective.
